name: Fu Mi
bio: Fu Mi is dated by Giles to the 3rd and 4th centuries AD. Giles prints two of his poems, both on the grief of separated lovers.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Lovers Parted
poems.author: Fu Mi

poems.title: After Parting
poems.author: Fu Mi
poems.text:
Thy chariot and horses have gone, and I fret
And long for the lover
I ne'er can forget.
O wanderer, bound in far countries to dwell,
Would I were thy shadow! —
I'd follow thee well.
And though clouds and though darkness my presence should hide,
In the bright light of day
I would stand by thy side!
